new_entities.name: CPAP for severe obstructive sleep apnea
aliases: continuous positive airway pressure for severe OSA
CPAP in severe obstructive sleep apnea
new_entities.description: Continuous positive airway pressure treatment used in adults with severe or at least moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea.

new_entities.name: Cardiovascular outcomes
new_entities.description: Major cardiovascular outcomes such as myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure events, vascular death, or composite cardiovascular endpoints.

edges.effect_quant: Across hard-outcome trials, CPAP has not clearly reduced major cardiovascular events in severe or moderate-to-severe OSA: pooled RR 0.77 in 10 trials, SAVE HR 1.10, and another 18-trial meta-analysis OR 0.84.
edges.population: adults with severe or at least moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea, often with established cardiovascular disease
edges.mechanism: CPAP reduces intermittent hypoxemia, sympathetic activation, and blood-pressure burden, but these physiologic gains have not translated consistently into fewer major cardiovascular events in minimally sleepy or only partly adherent trial populations.
edges.summary: This is a physiologically plausible but clinically contested edge. CPAP helps symptoms and some surrogate cardiovascular measures, yet randomized evidence for preventing hard cardiovascular events remains largely neutral.
edges.caveats: Several pivotal trials enrolled patients with low baseline sleepiness and average adherence near 3 to 4 hours per night. The evidence is stronger for symptom relief and modest blood-pressure improvement than for event prevention.

evidence.notes: Association of Positive Airway Pressure With Cardiovascular Events and Death in Adults With Sleep Apnea: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: major adverse cardiovascular events with positive airway pressure versus control across 10 sleep-apnea trials

evidence.citation: McEvoyRD et al 2016 N Engl J Med

effect_quant.comparator: primary composite cardiovascular endpoint with CPAP plus usual care versus usual care alone in SAVE
